prompts: On a private video call, make three faces that match your last three moods.
Stay seated on camera and do a ten-second dance with only your shoulders.
Use your hands on camera to act out the best part of your day without speaking.
On the call, copy my expression for five seconds, then make your own version.
Show your partner a safe, ordinary view from where you are sitting right now.
On camera, make a tiny victory pose for something you handled this week.
Use only your eyebrows to show how your day went; let me guess the story.
On the call, silently act out a hobby you enjoy and let your partner guess it.
Hold up one hand and show your current mood with a number from one to five.
On camera, mime how you look when you are trying not to laugh.
Make a slow, silly wave on the call as if you are greeting me from far away.
Show your partner a hand gesture you use often and explain what it means.
Stay seated and show three safe stretches you already know, at your own pace.
On camera, draw a shape in the air with one finger and let me name it.
Act out your favorite kind of weather using only your face and hands.
On the call, switch between your most serious face and your most relaxed one.
Use your hands to show the size of the best thing that happened today.
On camera, make a quiet sound for your mood and let me guess what it means.
Give your partner a slow thumbs-up, thumbs-sideways, or thumbs-down for today.
Show a simple hand movement that would make a good greeting for us.
On the call, make a face that shows how you feel about tomorrow.
Mime opening an invisible door into your ideal quiet evening.
Use your hands to act out a small thing you are looking forward to.
On camera, copy my hand shape, then change one part to make it yours.
Send a voice note telling the story of a small childhood win in under a minute.
Describe one family meal you remember, using the sounds you heard around it.
Record a voice note thanking someone who helped you when you were young.
Tell me a short story about a time you felt brave, even if nobody noticed.
Use a voice note to describe a place where you used to feel calm.
Tell the story of a mistake that became funny after some time passed.
Send a voice note naming a skill you want to learn and why it matters to you.
Describe a kind thing someone did for you, then say how you felt afterward.
Tell me about an ordinary day from your childhood that you still remember well.
Record one sentence in the voice you use when comforting someone you love.
Share a quick voice note about a choice you made that helped you grow.
Describe a family tradition you would like us to make our own someday.
Tell me what you thought your life would be like at this age when you were twelve.
Use a voice note to explain one value you learned from someone close to you.
Tell a short story about a time you helped someone and did not expect thanks.
Record the sound of your happiest laugh, then tell me what set it off.
Describe a place from your past that you would like to revisit with me on a call.
Send a voice note about a small thing you are proud of this month.
Tell me one family story you would like future generations to hear.
Describe a day when you felt welcomed somewhere new.
Share a voice note about a lesson you learned by watching, not being told.
Tell me one part of your background that people often misunderstand.
Record a short message about what makes a normal day feel good to you.
Tell me a story about a person who made you feel that you belonged.
Text me one belief about yourself that you are trying to change.
Write three lines about what gives you courage when you feel unsure.
Send a short list of what you want more of in your life this year.
Text the name of one value you want your choices to show, then explain why.
Write a note about a fear that has stopped you from trying something new.
Send a message about one way you are different from your family, in a good way.
Write the first line of a letter to your younger self, then send it to me.
Text one thing you wish people knew before judging how you handle stress.
Send a two-sentence picture of a future day that would make you feel content.
Write down one small promise you want to make to yourself this month.
Text a lesson you learned from a regret without blaming yourself for it.
Send one sentence about a part of your identity you want to understand better.
Write a short note on what being financially secure would mean to you.
Text a question about faith or belief that you are still thinking through.
Name a hard choice you made for your own well-being, then send the reason.
Send a message describing how you know you need rest before you burn out.
Write one thing you admire in someone close to you and one thing you learned.
Text a goal you are afraid to say out loud, with one first step toward it.
Send a short note about what makes you feel most like yourself.
Write a kind reply to a younger version of you who made a mistake.
Text one memory that taught you to speak up for yourself.
Send me one honest sentence about a change you want to make in your life.
Write down what you would keep the same if you could restart this year.
Text one question you would like us to make time to discuss soon.
On a private video call, name one boundary you want us to protect and ask for mine.
Let me finish one hard thing I want to say before you reply; then switch roles.
On the call, tell me one way I can make it easier to share difficult news.
Describe one kind of apology that helps you feel heard, then let me ask a question.
On camera, say one need you often hide; I will listen without trying to fix it.
Tell me how you prefer we handle it when one of us needs space.
On the call, name one fear about our future and one hope beside it.
Ask me a question about a boundary, then share your answer to the same question.
Describe a time you felt lonely while talking to someone, and what would have helped.
Tell me one way jealousy shows up for you, without asking either of us to change it now.
On the call, say what respect looks like when we disagree about money.
Share one part of a past relationship lesson that still affects your trust; no names needed.
Ask me what helps me feel cared for from far away, then answer for yourself.
Tell me what you need when you are upset but not ready to talk yet.
On camera, describe a moment when you felt unseen and what you wish I had noticed.
Say one thing you want us to do differently after our next disagreement.
Tell me what privacy means to you when two people are close.
Ask me which worry I keep quiet, then share one of your own if you want.
On the call, explain a boundary you learned to set later than you wish you had.
Tell me one fear that might affect us if we leave it unspoken.
Describe what a fair way to make a big shared choice would look like to you.
Say one thing that helps you trust my words when we cannot be together.
Ask me what makes it feel safe to disagree with you, then share your answer.
On the call, tell me how I can check in when you seem quiet without pushing.
Write a message about a truth you are still learning to accept about yourself.
Text one family pattern you are working hard not to carry into our future.
Send a note about a regret you want to answer with a different choice now.
Write what you would want me to know during the hardest week of your life.
Text one part of your past that still needs more kindness from you.
Send a message about a fear you want us to face as a team, at our own pace.
Write one thing you would want repaired between us if I could listen without arguing.
Text what being fully known by me would feel like, even if it is hard to explain.
Send a note about a loss you still wish you had more room to talk about.
Write what you need before we make a major choice that affects both of us.
Text one part of your identity you most want protected from judgment.
Send a message about something you hide because you fear it makes you hard to love.
Write one question you have been afraid to ask about our shared future.
Text what you want me to understand about your silence when you feel overwhelmed.
Send one honest sentence about how you feel in our relationship today.
Write what a safe disagreement would let you say that you hold back now.
Text a truth about money, family, or work that you want us to face together.
Send a note about a choice you wish you had made for yourself, not for approval.
Write what you would change about the way you learned to handle anger.
Text one fear about the future that you do not want to carry alone.
Send a message about what you need from me when you do not know what to ask for.
Write one promise you hope we can make only when we are both ready.
Text what you most want to feel safe bringing to me, and what would help.
Send a note saying what you hope I never assume about the part of you you protect.
